messages.subject: 2x4 Mixed design for developmental study
parts:
I am interested in using NBS to look at whole brain, network changes as a function of adolescent brain development. As I understand it, the current analysis framework does not support using mixed designs...? Specifically, we're interested only in the interaction between age (adolescent vs adult) and time (4 different scanning time points). 
Any suggestions?
Thanks,
Robin

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] 2x4 Mixed design for developmental study
parts:
Hi Robin,

That's correct, mixed effects models are not supported. I am actually
not aware of any studies that have done LME analysis and NBS in the
literature, but I have not looked explicitly for it, either.

It is definitely on my list of features to add, but it is not a
straightforward method. For example:
* "exchangeability blocks" would have to be added; I am sure the
functionality is present in other packages but I haven't looked into
it
* how to add a way to choose random effects structure flexibly.
There is debate over this topic. See e.g., "D.J. Barr et al., 2013"
and "H. Matuschek et al., 2017", both in J Memory Language.
* how to handle covariance structure
* which method to do model estimation
* how to calculate P-values and determine significance. There is
actually debate over this, see old threads on the R mailing list, and
also "S.G. Luke, 2017, Behavior Research Methods 49(4)"
* etc. ad nauseam

As far as I understand, these are also computationally/time-intensive
(which doesn't matter much if you have access to a cluster), but if I
were to use MCMC (not applicable w/ random slopes) or bootstrapping
for estimation, the number of computations would explode (i.e.,
multiply by the # of permutations and # of regions/edges tested).

I will most likely settle on the "lme4" package, whenever I get around
to implementing this stuff. You should check that package out; it has
several vignettes that might be helpful. There are also a lot of
helpful tutorials and presentations/lectures for LME analysis in R and
for learning the statistical concepts behind it.

Let me know if you have other questions.
Chris
